c.v: Standing at the edge of a bungee platform is frightening enough, but knowing that you have to jump is already terrifying. Now imagine that splash of water added to the experience – this makes traditional bungee jumping even more thrilling.

And that is the main reason to try Splash Bungee Rishikesh! Height, freefall, speed, and water create a combination that is hard to ignore for travelers who want something else besides sightseeing, cafés and river rafting.
What Is Splash Bungee?
Splash bungee
is the modification of bungee jumping that involves diving into a water-splash zone before the bungee cord pulls the participant up.

The adventure starts at the high platform where professionals secure the participant with appropriate harnesses. After that, it is time to jump. You will experience several seconds of complete freefall, see the ground rushing closer and the water appearing. After that, the cord will control the descent.
A 165-Foot Leap That Challenges Your Courage

Height is one of the elements that make splash bungee jumping so exciting. Thrill Factory offers bungee jumping from the 165-foot platform at its adventure facility located in Shivpuri, Rishikesh. Official activity listing features water splash availability, airbag safety and complimentary DSLR video of the jump.

Standing on a platform at 165 feet, you feel much taller. Confident participants also get frightened at the edge of the platform and start making excuses. Meanwhile, jump master encourages you to concentrate on the countdown.
Your main goal is taking the plunge and overcoming the fear that starts before the jump.
The Element of Water Adds to Excitement
Bungee jump itself is a thrilling experience
. However, in case of splash bungee jumping, water is another element that makes it even more exciting.

You will see the rapid approach of water in the middle of the fall. In addition to the fall, the approaching water is creating an additional adrenaline rush because your brain is trying to calculate the speed and the direction of your dive simultaneously.
Moreover, water splashing adds visual effect to your jump. Instead of a usual jump against landscape, it is much more dynamic and exciting one with the presence of water.
It Feels Terrifying and Liberating at the Same Time
Another exciting thing about bungee jumping is a quick change of emotions.

Before the jump, you can be nervous, unsure and even ready to give up. During the freefall, there is the feeling of weightlessness. After catching with the cord, fear changes into relief, excitement, and pride.

This unique emotional journey makes splash bungee jumping different from ordinary amusement rides. In the latter, you do not need to make the decision to leave the safety and start the descent yourself.
Professional Briefing and Safety Preparations

Of course, bungee jumping is a very thrilling experience, but it must be done with appropriate supervision and safety measures. At Thrill Factory, participants receive briefing, harness fitting and jump supervision from trained professionals. The bungee cord setup is adjusted according to the participant's weight, and the chest and ankle attachments are double-checked before the jump.
The platform was designed and built with assistance of professionals from the United Kingdom, according to the official Thrill Factory activity page.

Participants are advised to pay attention to every instruction, disclose their medical conditions and avoid doing the activity under peer pressure. It is much more exciting to prepare properly for the adventure.
Who Can Do Splash Bungee?
According to the official participation guidelines, the minimum age of participants is 12 years. For solo jumps, the weight limits vary from 40 kg to 120 kg.
Tandem bungee jumping is possible for the participants whose combined weight does not exceed 180 kg, including the harness.

Those who suffer from serious heart diseases, have recently undergone surgery, have severe problems with their back or neck, uncontrolled blood pressure, epilepsy or any other significant health issues should consult professional physician before going for bungee jumping.
It is recommended to wear comfortable clothes. Loose scarves and other accessories should not be worn, and it is necessary to avoid heavy food consumption before the jump.
Capture the Experience on Video

In spite of the fact that the freefall lasts only several seconds, sometimes people are unable to realize what exactly happens during it. Some of the participants say that they can only recall standing at the edge of the platform and landing on the ground afterwards.
Video will allow you to watch your experience later and see all the moments you have missed – hesitation at the edge, reaction during the jump and the moment of cord pulling you up.

Currently, Thrill Factory includes the complimentary DSLR video in their 165-foot bungee jumping activity. It is much more memorable and gives participants an opportunity to share the video with their relatives and friends.
Why Choose Splash Bungee in Rishikesh?
Rishikesh is already a place for high-energy outdoor activities. Including splash bungee in your itinerary will add a new and challenging experience.
It does not require long training. No previous experience of bungee jumping is needed. What you need is listening to professionals and trusting the safety process.
Thrill Factory's bungee experience
is located in Shivpuri and works from 10:00 AM to 9:00 PM, depending on operational conditions. The listed prices of the solo experience are ₹3,000, tandem one costs ₹6,000.
Take the Leap
Splash Bungee Rishikesh is not only a dive into water. It is the experience of confronting the voice in your head saying that you cannot do it.

Countdown can last for only several seconds, but achievement will stay with you for years. Once you take the plunge, feel the freefall and return to the solid ground, you will know why splash bungee is called one of the most thrilling adventure experiences in Rishikesh.
Sometimes, the only way to overcome your fear is not running away from it, but diving right into it.

description: Here's a confession from people who sell adventure activities for a living: ziplining is the one we recommend to the most people. c.v: Here's a confession from people who sell adventure activities for a living:
ziplining
is the one we recommend to the most people.

Bungee scares half our customers away before they even reach the platform. Rafting needs a free morning and a change of clothes. But a zipline? Ten-year-olds do it. Grandparents do it. People who swore they'd "just watch" end up doing it twice.

And Uttarakhand quietly has some of the best ziplines in India including one that flies you straight across the Ganga. Most travel blogs lump them all together as "ziplining," which is a bit like calling both a scooter and a superbike "two-wheelers." Technically true. Practically useless.
So here's the actual breakdown: every zipline in Uttarakhand worth doing in 2026, what each one really costs, and which one suits you.
First, the Quick Answer
If you're skimming (we know you are), here's the cheat sheet:
Now the details, because the details are where people waste money.
1. The Zipline Over the Ganga — Shivpuri, Rishikesh
This is the one. The longest zipline in Uttarakhand, roughly 750–800 metres of cable strung 70 metres above the Ganga, and the only zip in the state that takes you clean across the river.

You get harnessed, you get a short practice run on a baby 15-metre wire (everyone's nervous laugh happens here), and then you're off white water below, Himalayan foothills ahead, and a speed that touches triple digits on a good run. The whole thing, briefing included, takes about 45 minutes to an hour.
The numbers:

items.v: Cost: ₹1,400–2,000 per person depending on operator and season
Age: 10–12 years minimum (under-18s need a parent's signed consent, and a guardian along)
Weight: roughly 27–110 kg, varies slightly by operator
Timings: 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM
Location: Shivpuri, about 15 km from Rishikesh on the Badrinath road — same belt as the rafting and bungee operators

c.v: Is it worth ₹2,000 for under a minute of flying? We get asked this a lot, usually by someone comparing it to a ₹1,000 rafting trip that lasts two hours. Fair question. Our honest answer: rafting is a better activity, the zipline is a better moment. Crossing the Ganga in the air is one of those fifteen seconds your brain files away permanently. Also, the video is spectacular.
One practical note most people don't come to Shivpuri only for this. They raft in the morning, zipline after lunch, and it slots in perfectly because the zip needs way less time and zero stamina.
2. The Flying Fox — Mohan Chatti, Rishikesh
Different beast entirely, and people constantly confuse the two, so let's clear it up.
The Shivpuri zipline: you sit upright in a harness and glide. Civilised.

The Flying Fox at Mohan Chatti: you're strapped in face-down, Superman-style, hauled up a hillside, and then released to scream down a kilometre of cable at 120+ kmph over a Himalayan stream. Up to three people go at once, side by side, which means your friends' faces are part of the footage. This matters more than you'd think.
The numbers:

items.v: Cost: ₹2,500–3,800 standalone — but almost nobody books it standalone
The smart play: it's part of the bungee + giant swing + flying fox combo (₹8,000–9,400 total), and that combo is genuinely the best per-rupee adrenaline deal in north India
Same site as the famous bungee platforms, about 15–25 minutes from Tapovan
Weight range roughly 40–110 kg

c.v: If you're already going for the bungee, adding the Flying Fox is a no-brainer. If bungee isn't happening (no judgement), the Flying Fox alone still sends you home buzzing.
3. Sky Trek at Kempty Falls — Mussoorie
Mussoorie's best zip, and weirdly underrated because everyone goes to Kempty Falls for the waterfall and treats the zipline as an afterthought.

Don't. The Sky Trek — locals call it "Man vs Superman" runs about 600 feet across the Kempty gorge at a height of nearly 200 feet, hitting speeds around 80 kmph. For thirty-odd seconds, you've got the waterfall on one side, the valley dropping away below, and absolutely nothing to hold onto. In the best way.

Costs are friendly too: ₹500–1,000 depending on season and package. If you're doing the standard Mussoorie circuit (Mall Road, Gun Hill, Kempty), this adds a genuine thrill to an otherwise gentle sightseeing day.
4. Mussoorie Lake Zipline — The Family One

About 6 km before Mussoorie town, there's a short, sweet valley zipline at Mussoorie Lake — roughly 330 feet long, 70 feet up, speeds around 50 kmph. The whole thing is over in five or six minutes including the strapping-in.

At ₹500–600, this is the zipline for the family member who "doesn't do adventure stuff." Minimum age is about 10, the run is gentle, and the views over the valley are lovely. We've seen plenty of people do this one as a confidence-builder and book the Shivpuri Ganga zip for their next trip. It's a gateway drug, basically.

Nearby, Ikya Island adventure park (on the Dehradun–Mussoorie road) bundles ziplining with wall climbing, zorbing and a sky walk — combo passes run ₹1,000–2,400, decent value if you've got kids who need exhausting.
5. Dhanaulti and Kanatal — Zips on the Quiet Side

If you're doing the Mussoorie–Dhanaulti–Kanatal–Tehri road trip (and you should, it's gorgeous), the adventure parks along the way — Dhanaulti Eco Park and the Kanatal-area parks — all run short ziplines, usually alongside sky bridges and valley crossings.

These are ₹300–700 affairs. Short, scenic, fun. Nobody drives to Kanatal for the zipline, but stopping for one between deodar forests is exactly the kind of unplanned thing road trips are for. Some packages combine them with Tehri Lake water sports, which makes for a ridiculous day: zipline in the morning, jet ski by afternoon.
So Which One Should YOU Do?
Let's make it simple:

items.v: One trip, one zipline, maximum story value → Shivpuri's Ganga zipline. Nothing else in the state crosses the river.
You want to feel genuine fear → Flying Fox, face-down, in the combo with bungee.
Travelling with parents or young kids → Mussoorie Lake or the Dhanaulti parks.
Already in Mussoorie anyway → Kempty's Sky Trek. Best thrill-per-rupee in the hills.
Honeymoon / couple trip → Ganga zipline (some operators run tandem) plus a riverside camp night. You're welcome.

c.v: When to Go
Ziplines in Uttarakhand

run pretty much year-round, with one big exception: monsoon. From July to mid-September, the Rishikesh-belt zips shut down along with rafting — wet cables, poor visibility, slippery platforms, not worth anyone's time.
The sweet spots:

items.v: October–November: crisp air, post-monsoon greenery, clear Himalayan views. Our pick.
February–April: pleasant everywhere, all activities open, peak season energy in Rishikesh.
May–June: hot in Rishikesh by noon (book morning slots), but Mussoorie and Kanatal are lovely.
December–January: cold but totally doable. The hill-station zips with winter mist have their own charm. Carry a jacket; the wind chill at 80 kmph is real.

c.v: What to Wear and Carry (Learn From Others' Mistakes)

items.v: Closed shoes. Sneakers, sports shoes, anything with a back. We've watched more than one slipper sail into the Ganga. The slipper does not come back.
Fitted clothes — t-shirt and track pants beat anything loose or flowy. The harness sits on your waist and thighs.
Sunglasses with a strap, or keep them in your pocket. Same logic as the slippers.
Phone ONLY if it's strapped or zipped away. Most operators sell photo/video packages; in Shivpuri the footage is usually worth the few hundred rupees.
Skip it if you're pregnant or have serious heart, spine or knee issues — every operator will ask you to sign a declaration anyway, so be straight about it.

c.v: How to Reach the Zipline Hotspots

items.v: Rishikesh/Shivpuri: Fly into Jolly Grant, Dehradun (22 km from Rishikesh), or train to Haridwar/Yog Nagari Rishikesh. From Delhi by road it's about 240 km, 5–6 hours. Shivpuri is another 25–30 minutes upstream from Tapovan.
Mussoorie: Dehradun is your rail and air hub; Mussoorie is 35 km of switchbacks uphill from there. Kempty Falls is 15 km past Mussoorie.
Dhanaulti/Kanatal: About an hour beyond Mussoorie on the same road. Combine, don't make separate trips.

c.v: FAQs: What People Are Asking About Uttarakhand Ziplines in 2026

Where is the longest zipline in Uttarakhand? Shivpuri, near Rishikesh. The line runs roughly 750–800 metres across the Ganga at a height of about 70 metres — it's the only zipline in the state that crosses the river.

How much does ziplining cost in Uttarakhand? Anywhere from ₹300 to ₹3,800 depending on where and what. Hill-station park zips in Mussoorie, Dhanaulti and Kanatal run ₹300–1,000. The big Ganga zipline at Shivpuri costs ₹1,400–2,000. The face-down Flying Fox near Rishikesh is ₹2,500–3,800, cheapest inside a bungee combo.

What's the difference between a zipline and a flying fox? Mostly position and intensity. On a standard zipline you sit upright in a harness and glide. On the Flying Fox you're strapped face-down, superhero-style, and the Rishikesh version hits 120+ kmph over a 1 km run. Same physics, very different heart rate.

Is ziplining safe in Rishikesh? Yes, with registered operators. The Shivpuri and Mohan Chatti setups run on international-standard cables and harnesses, with trained instructors, practice runs, and double-checks before every release. Book through a verified operator and follow the briefing — that's genuinely all it takes.

Can kids do ziplining in Uttarakhand? Mostly yes. The minimum age is around 10 at most sites (12 at some), with a parent's signed consent and an accompanying adult required for under-18s. The Mussoorie Lake and Dhanaulti zips are the most kid-friendly; the Flying Fox is not for young children.

Is there a weight limit? Yes — typically between about 27–40 kg on the lower end and 100–130 kg on the upper end, depending on the site. Operators weigh you before the activity; it's a safety thing, not a formality.

Do I need any experience or fitness for ziplining? None. You're clipped in, gravity does the work. Basic fitness and the ability to follow a five-minute briefing is the entire entry requirement, which is exactly why we recommend it to people who find rafting or bungee too much.

Is ziplining open during monsoon? No. The Rishikesh-area ziplines close from July to mid-September along with rafting. Hill-station park zips may run on dry days but are weather-dependent. Plan for October onwards or before June.

Can I do rafting and ziplining on the same day? Easily and you should. The classic Shivpuri day is rafting in the morning (the 16 km stretch), lunch, then the Ganga zipline in the afternoon. The zip takes under an hour, so it slots in without any rush.

Zipline in Rishikesh or Mussoorie which is better? Different jobs. Rishikesh (Shivpuri) is the serious one longest, highest, over the Ganga, proper bragging rights. Mussoorie's zips are shorter, cheaper, and perfect as a fun add-on to a sightseeing trip. If you only do one in your life, do Shivpuri.
Uttarakhand's ziplines cover the full spectrum — from a ₹500 five-minute valley glide your mum will enjoy, to a face-down kilometre at 120 kmph that will rearrange your priorities.
Our advice hasn't changed in years: build your trip around Rishikesh, do the Ganga zipline at Shivpuri, add the Flying Fox if your nerves allow, and save the hill-station zips for the Mussoorie leg.

description: Discover the best things to do in Rishikesh — from white-water rafting and bungee jumping to ziplining, yoga, and Ganga Aarti. Complete 2025 travel guide by ThrilFactory.in, Uttarakhand's premier adventure destination.

c.v: By ThrilFactory.in | The Shivpuri Thrill Factory — Adventure Destination

Tucked into the foothills of the Garhwal Himalayas where the mighty Ganges descends from the mountains onto the plains, Rishikesh is one of India's most extraordinary destinations. It is at once a spiritual sanctuary, a yoga mecca, and the undisputed Adventure Capital of India — a rare combination that draws millions of travellers from across the globe every single year.

Whether you are an adrenaline junkie chasing your next thrill, a spiritual seeker searching for inner peace, a nature lover hungry for Himalayan landscapes, or simply a curious traveller looking for something different — Rishikesh delivers on every front. From heart-stopping white-water rapids and soaring ziplines to sacred evening rituals on the banks of the Ganges, this city has something for everyone.

In this comprehensive guide, we cover the best things to do in Rishikesh, complete with pricing, the best time to visit, insider tips, and everything you need to plan the perfect trip. And if you're ready to book your adventure,
ThrilFactory.in
is your one-stop destination for certified, world-class adventure experiences in Rishikesh and Uttarakhand.
Why Visit Rishikesh?

Rishikesh sits at an altitude of approximately 372 metres above sea level, where the Ganges river emerges from its mountain passage and flows onto the Indo-Gangetic plains. The city is flanked by dense forests, rugged gorges, and the first peaks of the Himalayas a geography that makes it naturally perfect for adventure sports.

Beyond adventure, Rishikesh has been a centre of Hindu pilgrimage and yogic tradition for thousands of years. The famous Beatles Ashram, where the Fab Four spent weeks studying Transcendental Meditation in 1968, is located here, a testament to the city's global spiritual influence. Today, Rishikesh hosts the world-famous International Yoga Festival every February, attracting practitioners and teachers from over 100 countries.
This unique blend of ancient tradition and modern adventure makes Rishikesh unlike any other destination in the world.
Quick Travel Facts

rows.v: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (35 km away)

c.v: Top 10 Best Things to Do in Rishikesh
1. White-Water River Rafting — The Crown Jewel of Rishikesh
If there is one activity that defines Rishikesh more than any other, it is
white-water river rafting
on the Ganges. Every year, tens of thousands of adventurers descend on Rishikesh specifically to experience the legendary rapids of the holy river — and it never disappoints.

The Ganges offers a range of rafting stretches to suit all skill levels, from gentle Grade 1–2 rapids perfect for beginners and families, to ferocious Grade 3–4+ rapids that will test even experienced rafters. The most popular stretch runs from Shivpuri to Rishikesh (16 km), typically taking 2–3 hours and passing through iconic rapids with names like The Wall, Three Blind Mice, Golf Course, and Roller Coaster.

For those seeking a longer, more intense expedition, the Marine Drive to Rishikesh stretch (36 km) is the gold standard — a full-day adventure through virtually untouched Himalayan terrain, passing towering cliffs, pristine beaches, and some of the most powerful rapids in India.

Rafting in Rishikesh is not just an adrenaline rush. Between the rapids, the river flows calmly past dense jungle, allowing you to absorb the breathtaking Himalayan scenery at your own pace. Many operators allow you to jump into the river from small cliffs along the way a bonus thrill at no extra cost.
Key Details:

items.v: Best Stretch: Shivpuri to Rishikesh (16 km) for beginners; Marine Drive to Rishikesh (36 km) for advanced rafters
Duration: 2–3 hours (short) | 5–6 hours (long stretch)
Best Season: September–November and February–May (avoid monsoon July–August)
Price Range: ₹600 – ₹2,500 per person depending on stretch
Age/Weight: Minimum age 14 years; no upper weight limit in most cases

c.v: Pro Tip: Book the early morning slot (7–8 AM) for calmer water levels, better visibility, and cooler temperatures. Avoid peak afternoon hours. Always choose a certified operator — safety equipment, trained guides, and rescue protocols make all the difference.
2. Bungee Jumping — South Asia's Highest Leap
For pure, unfiltered adrenaline, nothing in Rishikesh matches the experience of
bungee jumping
at Mohan Chatti. At a jaw-dropping 83 metres above the valley floor, this is the highest bungee jumping platform in South Asia — and one of the most professionally operated in all of Asia.

The platform is perched on a dramatic cantilever structure above a river gorge, surrounded by dense forest and mountains. When you step off the edge, there is a moment of absolute silence before the world rushes up to meet you at speed — and then the bungee cord brings you soaring back up, the valley spinning below your feet.

The facility is operated by Jumping Heights, India's most reputed extreme sports company, using internationally certified equipment and safety standards. Every jumper goes through a thorough safety briefing, and trained staff handle all equipment checks and supervision.
Key Details:

items.v: Height: 83 metres (South Asia's highest bungee jump!)
Weight Limit: 40 kg minimum, 110 kg maximum
Duration: Half day including briefing, gear fitting, and the jump
Price Range: ₹3,500 – ₹4,500 per person
Location: Mohan Chatti, approximately 15 km from Rishikesh

c.v: Pro Tip: Book your slot at least 2–3 days in advance during the peak season (October–November). The facility often sells out. Wear comfortable, athletic clothing and remove all loose accessories before the jump.
3. Ziplining — Soar Above the Ganges
Ziplining in Rishikesh

has emerged as one of the most exhilarating and accessible adventure experiences in Uttarakhand. Imagine being harnessed to a cable and launched over the Ganges river and the surrounding jungle at speeds of up to 120 km/h — the trees rushing below you, the mountains stretching in every direction, and the river glittering far beneath your feet.

Multiple zipline operators run high-quality experiences near Laxman Jhula and Shivpuri, with cables stretching up to 200 metres across river gorges and treetops. Some operators offer tandem ziplining, so couples and friends can fly side by side.

What makes Rishikesh ziplining special compared to other locations is the setting. You are not flying over a theme park or a manicured resort — you are soaring through one of the most beautiful river valleys in the Himalayas, with the sacred Ganges below and ancient mountains all around. It is a genuine, immersive Himalayan adventure.
ThrilFactory.in
offers exclusive zipline packages in Rishikesh — including combo deals with river rafting that give you the best value for your adventure budget.
Key Details:

items.v: Speed: Up to 120 km/h
Cable Length: Up to 200 metres
Weight Limit: Typically 25 kg – 100 kg (varies by operator)
Location: Shivpuri and Laxman Jhula area
Price Range: ₹600 – ₹1,200 per person
Duration: Approximately 1–2 hours including briefing and gear

c.v: Pro Tip: Book a combo package (ziplining + rafting) through
ThrilFactory.in
for the best value. Wear fitted clothing and closed-toe shoes. Arrive early to beat the crowds and get the clearest views.
4. Giant Swing — India's Most Unique Thrill
If bungee jumping feels too vertical and ziplining feels too horizontal, the
Giant Swing
at Rishikesh might be the perfect middle ground — and in many ways, it is the most intense experience of all three.

Also operated by Jumping Heights at Mohan Chatti, the Giant Swing works by securing you in a full-body harness and then launching you in a sweeping arc across a river gorge, reaching speeds of up to 160 km/h — faster than even most bungee jumps. The sensation is a unique combination of free-fall terror and lateral G-force, swinging you out over the valley in a massive pendulum arc with the ground hundreds of feet below.
Many visitors who have done all three — bungee, zipline, and giant swing — report that the Giant Swing produces the longest-lasting rush of all.
Key Details:

items.v: Height: 83 metres above the valley floor
Speed: Up to 160 km/h
Weight Limit: 40 kg – 100 kg
Price Range: ₹3,500 – ₹4,000 per person

c.v: Pro Tip: Combo the Giant Swing with bungee jumping on the same day for a discounted rate. The two experiences complement each other perfectly — do the swing first if you want to "warm up" before the vertical drop!
5. Camping by the Ganges — Sleep Under the Himalayan Stars

For a completely different kind of adventure, camping on the banks of the Ganges near Rishikesh is one of the most memorable experiences you can have in all of India. The most popular camping areas are at Shivpuri Beach (15 km from Rishikesh) and Byasi — both located on sandy river banks flanked by jungle and mountains.

A typical Rishikesh camping package includes accommodation in a pitched tent (ranging from basic dome tents to Swiss cottage tents with proper beds), all meals around a campfire, and a variety of adventure activities. Evenings are spent around the bonfire with guitar, singing, and the sound of the Ganges flowing nearby. Mornings begin with bird song, river mist, and the distant peaks of the Himalayas catching the first light of dawn.
Many camps also offer yoga sessions at sunrise, which — surrounded by the Himalayan landscape — is an experience that genuinely changes people.
Key Details:

items.v: Best Spots: Shivpuri Beach (15 km) and Byasi (22 km from Rishikesh)
Best Season: October–June (avoid July–August monsoon)
Includes: Tent, all meals, campfire, evening activities
Price Range: ₹1,200 – ₹3,500 per person per night (varies by tent type)

c.v: Pro Tip: Upgrade to a Swiss cottage tent if you want genuine comfort — they come with proper beds, fans, and electric points. Book a package that includes river rafting for the best value. Carry a light jacket even in summer — nights by the river can be surprisingly cool.
6. Yoga and Meditation — The Spiritual Heart of Rishikesh

No guide to Rishikesh would be complete without a deep focus on yoga and meditation — arguably the most famous offering of this city on the global stage. Rishikesh is recognised worldwide as the Yoga Capital of the World, and for good reason.

The city is home to dozens of ashrams and yoga centres ranging from basic community spaces to world-class retreat facilities. Some of the most famous include Parmarth Niketan (Asia's largest ashram, situated directly on the Ganges), Sivananda Ashram (founded by the legendary Swami Sivananda), and Anand Prakash Yoga Ashram, which regularly features in international yoga publications.

Experiences range from single drop-in morning yoga classes on the riverbank (often free or very cheap) to intensive week-long or month-long residential retreats covering all aspects of traditional yoga philosophy, pranayama, and meditation.

The annual International Yoga Festival, held every February at Parmarth Niketan, is one of the largest yoga gatherings in the world — attracting over 1,000 practitioners and teachers from more than 100 countries for a week of classes, workshops, and ceremonies.
Key Details:

items.v: Famous Centres: Parmarth Niketan, Sivananda Ashram, Anand Prakash, Rishikesh Yog Peeth
Duration: Single sessions to multi-week residential retreats
Best Season: Year-round (October–April most pleasant)
Price Range: Free (drop-in ghat classes) to ₹25,000+ for full retreat packages

c.v: Pro Tip: Attend the free evening Ganga Aarti at Parmarth Niketan regardless of your interest in yoga. It takes place every day at sunset and is one of the most moving, beautiful ceremonies in all of India.
7. Kayaking on the Ganges

For those who want a more personal, intimate connection with the Ganges than rafting provides, kayaking is an outstanding alternative. Sit-in kayaks put you right at water level, with far more control and manoeuvrability than a raft — giving you a completely different perspective on the river.

Rishikesh offers both flatwater kayaking (perfect for beginners, families, and those who simply want to enjoy the scenery at their own pace) and whitewater kayaking through rapids for more experienced paddlers. Evening flatwater kayaking sessions, when the Ganges catches the setting sun and the mountains glow amber and gold, are particularly magical.
Key Details:

items.v: Best Location: Shivpuri Ghat and Marine Drive
Duration: 2–4 hours
Skill Level: Beginner and advanced options
Price Range: ₹1,500 – ₹3,500 per person

c.v: Pro Tip: Try an evening flatwater kayaking session for the most scenic experience. The light on the river at golden hour, with the mountains behind you and the Ganges stretching ahead, is genuinely unforgettable.
8. Trek to Neer Garh Waterfall

One of the best short treks near Rishikesh leads to the beautiful Neer Garh Waterfall, just 3 km from Laxman Jhula. The trail winds through dense mixed jungle, crossing small natural streams and passing under a canopy of ancient trees before emerging at a stunning two-tiered waterfall that cascades down moss-covered rocks into a clear natural pool.

The trek is accessible for all fitness levels and takes approximately 1.5–2 hours for the round trip. It's a perfect half-day excursion that combines gentle exercise with genuine natural beauty ideal for families, couples, and solo travellers who want a break from the more intense adventure activities.
Key Details:

items.v: Distance: 3 km from Laxman Jhula (6 km round trip)
Duration: 1.5–2 hours return
Difficulty: Easy to Moderate
Entry Fee: ₹50 – ₹100 per person

c.v: Pro Tip: Visit early morning (before 9 AM) to have the falls almost entirely to yourself. The jungle is alive with bird calls at that hour and the light through the forest canopy is spectacular. Wear waterproof shoes — the trail can be slippery near the water.
9. Laxman Jhula & Ram Jhula — The Icons of Rishikesh

No visit to Rishikesh is complete without spending time at the city's two most iconic landmarks: Laxman Jhula and Ram Jhula — the famous suspension bridges that span the Ganges and have become symbols of the city itself.

Laxman Jhula (1 km from Rishikesh) is the older of the two, a narrow iron suspension bridge swaying gently above the swift-flowing Ganges. According to Hindu legend, this is the exact spot where Lord Lakshmana crossed the river using a jute rope bridge. The current iron bridge, originally built in 1929, has recently been replaced by a modern structure — but the spiritual significance and spectacular views remain unchanged.
Right next to Laxman Jhula stands the extraordinary 13-storey Trayambakeshwar Temple, a wedding cake-like structure visible from miles around, its various floors dedicated to different Hindu deities.

Ram Jhula (3 km from Rishikesh) is longer and wider, and its surrounding area is home to some of Rishikesh's most famous ashrams, including Sivananda and Parmarth Niketan. The ghats below Ram Jhula are popular for bathing, meditation, and the evening Ganga Aarti ceremonies.
Both bridges are surrounded by vibrant bazaars selling everything from Rudraksha beads and Himalayan herbs to yoga pants and adventure gear — perfect for souvenir shopping.

Pro Tip: Visit Laxman Jhula at sunrise for an almost mystical experience — the mist rises from the river, sadhus perform their morning rituals on the ghats, and the mountains glow in the early light. It's one of those rare moments that feels genuinely timeless.
10. Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat — A Ceremony That Moves the Soul

Every evening as the sun sinks behind the Himalayan foothills, thousands of people gather at Triveni Ghat — the holiest bathing ghat in Rishikesh — for the nightly Ganga Aarti ceremony. This ancient ritual of fire worship offered to the Goddess Ganga is performed by young priests in orange robes, who swing enormous brass lamps in precise, choreographed patterns while chanting ancient Sanskrit hymns.

The sight of hundreds of oil lamps (diyas) being floated out on the dark Ganges, the sounds of bells and conch shells echoing off the river banks, and the smell of incense rising into the mountain air — it is an experience that transcends religion and moves even the most secular of travellers.
The ceremony typically begins around 6:00–6:30 PM and lasts approximately 45 minutes to an hour. Entry is completely free and open to everyone regardless of religion or nationality.
Key Details:

items.v: Location: Triveni Ghat, Rishikesh
Timings: Daily at sunset (approximately 6:00–7:00 PM, varies by season)
Entry: Free, open to all
Duration: 45 minutes to 1 hour

c.v: Pro Tip: Arrive at least 30 minutes early to secure a good viewing spot near the front — the ghat fills up quickly. If you want the most immersive experience, sit close to the river's edge rather than behind the barriers. Consider floating a diya yourself — it costs just a few rupees from vendors nearby and is a beautiful act of participation.
Best Time to Visit Rishikesh
Rishikesh is a year-round destination, but different seasons offer very different experiences:

All activities fully operational — book well in advance

c.v: Our Recommendation: Visit in October–November for the absolute best weather, clearest skies, and the widest range of adventure activities. February is ideal if you want to attend the International Yoga Festival.
How to Reach Rishikesh

By Air: The nearest airport is Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approximately 35 km away). It receives direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai, and other major Indian cities. Taxis from the airport to Rishikesh take about 45–60 minutes.

By Train: Rishikesh Railway Station is well-connected to Delhi (Haridwar Junction is the main railhead — 25 km away with frequent local buses and taxis onward to Rishikesh). The overnight train from Delhi Anand Vihar to Haridwar is a popular and comfortable option.

By Road: Rishikesh is approximately 240 km from Delhi (National Highway 58), a journey of 5–6 hours by car or bus. State-run buses (ISBT Kashmiri Gate, Delhi) and private Volvo coaches connect Delhi to Rishikesh multiple times daily.
Where to Stay in Rishikesh
Rishikesh offers accommodation for every budget:
Budget (₹500 – ₹1,500/night): Zostel Rishikesh, Bunk Stays Rishikesh, Madpackers Hostel — all popular with backpackers and solo travellers, excellent for meeting fellow adventurers.
Mid-Range (₹2,000 – ₹6,000/night): Hotel Dev Lok, Hotel Anand Lok, The Atali Ganga (riverside), Saptrishi Resort — comfortable rooms, good food, excellent locations near the ghats or river.
Luxury (₹10,000+/night): Glasshouse on the Ganges, Taj Rishikesh Resort & Spa, Ananda in the Himalayas — world-class facilities in stunning natural settings.
Unique: Riverside tent camps at Shivpuri (₹1,200 – ₹3,500/night) — one of the most magical accommodation experiences in India, sleeping by the Ganges under a star-filled Himalayan sky.
Essential Travel Tips for Rishikesh

items.v: Carry Valid ID: A government-issued photo ID is mandatory for all adventure sports bookings in Uttarakhand.
Respect the Local Culture: Rishikesh is a holy city. Dress modestly when visiting ashrams and temples. Leather items (shoes, belts) may not be permitted inside some religious spaces.

Rishikesh is Vegetarian: The city operates under a vegetarian and alcohol-free policy (officially — though riverside camps sometimes bend the rules). Embrace the incredible variety of local vegetarian food.
Book Adventure Activities in Advance: During the peak season (October–November), popular activities like bungee jumping, camping, and rafting can sell out days ahead. Use

Pack Smart: Comfortable athletic wear, waterproof shoes, a light fleece or jacket for evenings, high-SPF sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle are essentials.
Bargain Respectfully in Markets: Prices in the bazaars near Laxman Jhula and Ram Jhula are often inflated for tourists. Polite bargaining is expected and normal.
Stay Hydrated: Especially if doing multiple adventure activities in a day. The mountain air and physical exertion can deplete you faster than you expect.

Don't Swim Alone in the Ganges: The river looks deceptively calm in places but has powerful undercurrents. Only swim near designated bathing ghats and always with a life jacket during adventure activities.

Rishikesh is one of those rare places in the world that genuinely lives up to — and often exceeds — its reputation. That is what Thrill Factory in Shivpuri, Rishikesh does to people.

If you have been sitting on the fence about whether to finally do a bungee jump — or if you have already done one and want to push further — this is everything you need to know about the activities, the experience, and what to honestly expect when you show up.
Why Everyone Ends Up in Rishikesh for Bungee Jumping
Here is something worth understanding before we get into the activities.
Rishikesh — and specifically the Shivpuri stretch along the Ganga — is not just popular for
bungee jumping

because it looks good on Instagram. The geography here is genuinely exceptional. Deep gorges, dramatic elevation, rocky cliffs, and a river running below create the kind of natural setup that professional adventure engineers look for. You cannot recreate this with a crane in a city parking lot.

Thrill Factory sits right in the middle of this landscape, near the Indian Oil Petrol Pump on the Devprayag road in Shivpuri — about 12 kilometres from Tapovan. When you arrive, the first thing you notice is not the equipment or the platforms. It is the view. Mountains on every side, the sound of the Ganga in the distance, forest as far as you can see. Before you have even put on a harness, the place has already done something to your nervous system.
Every Activity at Thrill Factory — What It Actually Feels Like
Bungee Jumping —
This is the main event. A genuine 165-foot drop from a fixed platform, with a water splash landing zone and air bag safety system below. Free DSLR video is included so you have proof of what you did.

Here is what nobody tells you about the moment before a bungee jump: the fear is not really about the fall. It is about the decision to fall. The platform is solid under your feet. You are secure. Nothing is making you jump. You have to choose to step into thin air. That decision — that deliberate leap into the unknown — is what makes
bungee jumping
unlike any other experience.
Once you are in the air, the fear disappears instantly. There is simply no room for it.
Best for first-timers who want the real thing. Not a toned-down version, not a simulation. The actual experience, done properly.
Free Style Bungee —
If regular bungee is jumping off the edge,
Free Style Bungee
is making the jump your own.

Same height, same cord, same rush — but here you decide how you go. Dive headfirst. Spread your arms wide. Do a backflip if you have the nerve. The platform gives you a stunning panoramic view of the Himalayan landscape right up until the second you launch, and the jump is yours to shape however you want.

Most people who come back to Thrill Factory for a second visit choose Free Style Bungee. It is the version you do when you already know you can handle the fear and you just want to enjoy the art of the fall.
Age: 12 and above | Weight: 40 kg to 100 kg | Height: Minimum 4.5 feet
Rope Bungee —
Not everyone in your group is going to be ready for a full bungee jump. That is completely okay — and Rope Bungee is exactly why.

At 160 feet, you still get a significant, proper drop from a real height. The difference is that instead of an elastic cord, a rope controls your descent in a more gradual, smooth way. The free fall is real. The height is real. But the rebound is gentler, and the body does not take the same G-force as traditional bungee.

It is a brilliant option if you are nervous, if it is genuinely your first time, or if you simply want to test your relationship with heights before committing to the full jump. And at ₹1,500 with a free DSLR video included, it is one of the best value activities on the menu.
Reverse Bungee —
This one catches people off guard — and that is exactly the point.

With bungee jumping, you have time to build up to the moment. You walk to the edge. You look down. You breathe. You prepare. With Reverse Bungee, none of that happens. You are locked into a cage at ground level. You sit there for a moment, heart hammering, watching the mechanism load. And then — without warning — you are launched 180 feet into the air in two seconds flat.
Two seconds. 180 feet. Straight up.

The people who claim they are too scared to do a bungee jump often end up loving Reverse Bungee the most, because there is no agonising decision at the edge. The machine removes the choice entirely and just sends you skyward. Many visitors say the upward launch feels more intense than any downward fall.
Experience the world from 180 feet above — in the time it takes to blink.

SCAD is a free fall. No cord. No elastic. No rope. You are released from height and fall completely freely through the air until a precisely calibrated net catches you below. The net is there. It works. But your brain has a very hard time accepting that when you are standing at the release point looking down.

The gap between knowing you are safe and feeling like you are safe — that gap is where SCAD lives. It is not for everyone. But for anyone who has already done bungee and found themselves thinking "what's next?" — this is your answer.

You are harnessed and swung in a massive pendulum arc across the gorge — back and forth, the entire valley sweeping past you on every pass, the wind rushing, the Ganga glinting below. You are not falling. You are flying. And you stay up there long enough to actually look around and take in what is happening to you.

Giant Swing

If you are coming with a group where some people want intensity and others want something they can genuinely enjoy rather than just survive — put the Giant Swing on the list for everyone.
Age: 12 and above | Timing: 10 AM to 9 PM | From ₹1,500
Zip Lining —
2,000 | 800 Metres
After everything else — the drops, the launches, the free falls — Zip Lining feels like a reward.

800 metres of open air, soaring horizontally across the Shivpuri landscape with the forested hills on either side and the Ganga somewhere far below. You are moving fast enough to feel the wind properly but oriented in a way that lets you actually look around and appreciate where you are.
Most people do

Price: ₹2,000 | Distance: 800 metres | Timing: 10 AM to 7 PM
The Combo Packages — Because Why Do One Thing When You Can Do Three
If you are making the trip to Shivpuri, it genuinely does not make sense to do just one activity. Thrill Factory's combo packages bundle the best experiences together at a meaningfully lower price.

Archery + Box Cricket + Bowling. The perfect option for groups where not everyone is ready for extreme activities, or as an easy warm-up before heading into the jump zones. Genuinely fun even if you never go near a bungee platform.
Before You Go — The Honest Safety Talk
Nobody enjoys reading safety disclaimers. But this one matters, so please read it.

Thrill Factory's activities are run by trained professionals with proper equipment and established safety systems. The bungee uses both a water splash zone and an air bag below. The SCAD uses a precisely measured net. Every harness is fitted by staff before each activity. This is not a pop-up operation — it is a serious adventure facility.

That said, there are conditions that genuinely prevent participation, and hiding them does not make anyone safer — it just creates unnecessary risk. If you have a heart condition, high blood pressure, epilepsy, back or neck injuries, or are pregnant, these activities are not suitable for you. The health declaration at registration is not a formality. Fill it in honestly.

A few practical things worth knowing: wear closed sports shoes, not sandals or flip-flops. Remove loose jewellery and accessories before your activity. Do not arrive after drinking alcohol — you will not be allowed to participate. And please, eat something light a couple of hours before — not a full meal, but do not show up on an empty stomach either.

When to Visit

October to March is the sweet spot. The weather is clear, the air is cool and crisp on the platform, and the mountains in the background are at their most dramatic. This is also peak season, so book your slots in advance — especially on weekends and around public holidays.

April to June is warmer but still perfectly fine for most activities. July and August bring the monsoon, and while some activities may still run on clear days, the combination of rain, wet surfaces, and the generally unpredictable weather means you will get a much better experience if you plan your visit outside the monsoon window.
How to Reach Thrill Factory

I have never done anything like this before. Is Thrill Factory right for me?

Yes. Genuinely. The staff at Thrill Factory work with first-timers every single day. Nobody is going to rush you, mock you for being nervous, or make you feel like you do not belong there. Start with Rope Bungee or the standard Bungee Jump, follow the briefing carefully, and trust the process.

Comfortable clothes you can move freely in. Closed sports shoes are mandatory. Leave the flip-flops and heels in the car.
One Last Thing
Here is what I want you to take away from all of this.

Fear is normal. Wanting to back out the night before is normal. Standing on the platform and thinking "what on earth am I doing" is completely, utterly normal. Every person who has ever jumped off a bungee platform has had some version of that thought.
And every single one of them jumped anyway. And not one of them regretted it.

What Is Bungee Jumping and How Does It Work?
Bungee jumping involves leaping from a height while connected to a strong elastic cord. As you fall, the cord stretches and then recoils, slowing you down safely before pulling you back upward.
Modern bungee setups use advanced equipment, including:

items.v: High-strength elastic cords
Body harnesses and ankle straps
Professional safety systems

c.v: When handled by trained professionals, the entire process is designed to minimize risk.
Common Myths About Bungee Jumping
Let’s look at some of the most popular misconceptions that often scare first-timers.
Myth 1: The Rope Can Snap Anytime
This is one of the biggest fears people have. Many imagine the cord breaking mid-jump.
Reality:
Bungee cords are made from multiple layers of latex and are tested to handle weights far beyond human capacity. They undergo strict quality checks and are regularly replaced.
The chances of a properly maintained cord snapping are extremely low.
Myth 2: People Often Get Seriously Injured
Some believe that injuries are common in bungee jumping.
Reality:
Serious injuries are very rare when safety protocols are followed. Most reported issues happen due to human error or unregulated operators.
Professional operators follow strict guidelines, making the activity much safer than people assume.
Myth 3: Your Spine or Neck Will Get Damaged
Many people worry that the sudden jerk could harm their spine or neck.
Reality:
The bungee cord is designed to stretch gradually, reducing the impact. Proper harnessing ensures your body weight is evenly distributed, minimizing strain.
As long as you follow instructions, the risk is minimal.
Myth 4: It’s Not Safe for First-Timers
Beginners often feel that bungee jumping is only for experienced thrill-seekers.
Reality:
Most jumpers are actually first-timers. Operators provide clear instructions, safety briefings, and trained staff to guide you through every step.
You don’t need prior experience to enjoy your first jump safely.
Facts About Bungee Jumping Safety
Now let’s focus on the truth backed by facts and industry practices.
Fact 1: Strict Safety Standards Are Followed
Reputable bungee jumping operators follow international safety standards. Equipment is regularly inspected, and staff are trained in emergency procedures.
Many locations also require certifications and compliance checks to operate legally.
Fact 2: Double Safety Systems Are Used
Most setups include backup systems such as:

items.v: Double harnesses
Secondary safety ropes
Redundant attachment points

c.v: This ensures that even in rare cases of equipment failure, there is an extra layer of protection.
Fact 3: Weight and Health Checks Matter
Before jumping, participants must meet certain criteria, including:

items.v: Weight limits
Age requirements
Health conditions

items.v: Equipment is properly secured
Instructions are clearly followed
Safety protocols are maintained

c.v: This significantly reduces the chances of error.
Risks You Should Be Aware Of
While bungee jumping is generally safe, it’s important to understand the potential risks:

items.v: Minor injuries like bruises or strains
Dizziness or temporary disorientation
Rare cases of equipment or human error

c.v: However, these risks are minimal when jumping with certified operators.

Always go with a trusted and well-reviewed company that follows proper safety standards.
Follow Instructions Carefully
Listen to the staff and follow every guideline they provide.
Check Your Health Condition
Avoid jumping if you have heart problems, high blood pressure, or serious medical conditions.
Wear Comfortable Clothing
Avoid loose items and wear secure footwear for a safe experience.

The short answer is yes—bungee jumping is safe when done under professional supervision and with proper equipment.
Most fears surrounding the activity are based on myths rather than facts. With strict safety measures, advanced gear, and trained professionals, the risks are kept extremely low.
